To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

self-mention is a rhetorical strategy used to promote the author's work, that the strategy is used more often by authors who have higher status, that the strategy has more effect in some disciplines than in others, and that the strategy is more likely to be used by authors who are trying to promote their own work rather than the work of others.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of author self-mention in academic publication.
the rhetorical and epistemological dimensions of self-mention.
the ways in which authors construct and maintain their identities and credibility in their academic writing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-citation and self-mention are not only a way of citing oneself but also a way of citing others and the discipline.

the use of self-mention in academic publication is an essential part of the rhetorical strategies of academics, and the ways in which this is used are closely linked to the disciplinary norms and epistemic values of the disciplines in which academics work.

the use of self-mention is a rhetorical strategy that can be used to promote an author's work, but that this strategy can only be understood in terms of the epistemological assumptions of the discipline in which it is practiced and in terms of the wider context of self-promotion that is a feature of academic publishing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self-mention is an important rhetorical device for establishing and maintaining the credibility of knowledge claims in academic publication.
self-citation and self-mention are rhetorical practices that are not inherently positive or negative, but rather serve to promote a particular kind of academic authorship and knowledge production.
the self is an integral part of academic knowledge claims and self-citation is an important means for authors to promote their own work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
author self-reference is a complex and multifaceted practice that cannot be reduced to a single, negative meaning.
self-mention is a complex rhetorical strategy that should not be dismissed as mere egotism.
self-citation and self-mention are not necessarily problematic, nor are they always self-aggrandizing.
